answer.answer: Chevron completed its acquisition of Hess Corporation on July 18, 2025, and the aggregate purchase price was approximately $48 billion, including 15.38 million shares of Hess common stock bought in open market transactions in the first quarter of 2025 and 301.25 million shares of Chevron common stock issued as closing consideration [1]. As part of the transaction, Chevron assumed debt with an aggregate outstanding principal value of $8.8 billion [1]. The acquisition was accounted for as a business combination under ASC 805, and as a result of measuring the assets acquired and liabilities assumed at fair value, there was no goodwill or bargain purchase recognized [1]. Hess's legacy reserves are reviewed by legacy Hess staff with input from Chevron's RAC, and DeGolyer and MacNaughton audited the legacy Hess proved reserves, which represent approximately 13 percent of Chevron's total proved reserves [2]. Chevron's 10-K notes that Hess's total assets and total revenues represent 24 percent and 3 percent, respectively, of the related consolidated financial statement amounts [3]. Chevron's 10-K also states that the success of the Hess acquisition depends on its ability to realize anticipated benefits, including run-rate cost synergies, estimated five-year production and free cash flow growth rates, and higher shareholder returns [4].

answer.answer: On September 8, 2025, PTFI experienced an external mud rush incident at the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine that resulted in seven fatalities [1][2]. Approximately 800,000 metric tons of wet material entered the mine from the former Grasberg open pit and traveled rapidly to multiple levels, including a service level where seven team members were later found deceased [3]. Mining operations were temporarily suspended to prioritize recovery of the seven team members and to conduct investigations [1]. In late October 2025, PTFI restarted operations at the unaffected DMLZ and Big Gossan underground mines, while a phased restart of the Grasberg Block Cave mine is anticipated to begin in second-quarter 2026 [1][4].
